items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Roger Wolfe Kahn's father was the famous financier, Otto Kahn

ctx.x: So, Floyd O'Brien and I got on a bus, you know, the trombone player, and came to join Mezzrow. And we stayed, he had a house up in the Bronx, or up near -- yes, the Bronx, I was going to say near Harlem, but it was way up 167th Street, I think, and he had this big apartment where we stayed, we had no money or anything and we were just rehearsing, and Mezzrow was feeding us and what not, and as I say, the thing didn't take, I mean, with all the help of people like Benny Carter and Alex and what not, the thing…

And I think the first one was with Roger Wolfe Kahn. Now, as you know, Roger Wolfe Kahn's father was the famous financier, Otto Kahn, and every time we got a job the owners of the club found that Roger was the

son of one of the richest men in the world, Otto Kahn, so they would try to get Roger to buy the nightclub or restaurant which Roger refused to do, so that would be the end of our job and I said that being this wealthy was an obstacle in the way of getting work, because I was only with him about six months and we had about three jobs in the six months.
